A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hybrid Replay research and contain 14 readable pages with complete text, equations, algorithms, figures, and tables. Both end with references; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original benchmark experiments, ablations, and memory/forgetting analyses on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-Subset, and TinyImageNet, documented in Tables 2-3 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments, ablations, and memory/forgetting results in Section 5, Tables 2-3, and Figure 3. Retained original results qualify despite no new experiments being added.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithms 1-2 retain the same customized autoencoder, latent exemplar replay, synthetic replay, Lennard-Jones centroid alignment, distillation losses, and classification procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-100, ImageNet-Subset, and TinyImageNet under the same five FCIL configurations. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2-3 and Figure 3. Table 3 still compares HR with GeoDL, SS-IL, and GLFC; the added related-work citation does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 5 retains the same task/client configurations, data allocation with alpha = 1, ResNet-18 encoder, four-layer CNN decoder, and SGD training. Table 3's exemplar counts, memory budgets, and epoch counts are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains the same reduced-memory, latent/perfect-exemplar, knowledge-distillation, global-replay, and RFA ablations. Figure 3's memory sensitivity and forgetting analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over ten random initializations with SEMs in Section 5 and Table 2. No repeated-run information, uncertainty reporting practice, or statistical procedure changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and findings in Tables 2-3 and Figure 3 are unchanged. For example, Table 2 reports HR accuracy of 65.84 ± 0.57 on CIFAR-100 (10/10/50/5) in both versions.

T1.justification: The FCIL formulation and derivations in Section 3, Equations 1-6, and the loss and centroid-alignment mathematics in Equations 7-9 are unchanged. No assumptions, proofs, or formal properties are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about formalizing local/global forgetting, addressing both through HR, and outperforming baselines while preserving privacy with low memory and compute requirements.

C2.justification: The explanations of replay effectiveness, memory diversity, and privacy-performance tradeoffs remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the same decoder-capacity limitations concerning replay quality, memorization, privacy, and computational cost.

D1.justification: Implementation and training details in Section 5 and resource budgets and runtimes in Table 3 are unchanged. No new technical instructions or code/data access information are provided.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Khademi Nori and Kim (2025) to the citation supporting the definition of class-incremental learning, with a corresponding bibliography entry. The surrounding discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The displayed author name changes from Guanghui (Richard) Wang to Guanghui Wang, and a funding acknowledgment naming NSERC and the Rogers Cybersecure Catalyst Fellowship Program is added before the references. Scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added citation and acknowledgment cause minor text and reference reflow, with spacing adjustments around Table 3 on page 10. Figures, axes, legends, captions, and table structures retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: v3 adds a background citation and funding acknowledgment and makes small author-name and layout edits. These modest documentation changes do not materially alter the scientific argument, evidence, reproducibility, or readability; overall paper quality remains essentially unchanged.
